title: Motif-Consistent Counterfactuals with Adversarial Refinement for Graph-level Anomaly Detection

problem.claim: Graph-level anomaly detection seeks improved detection performance and generalization through causal counterfactual graphs.

gap.claim: Existing perturbation-based counterfactual generation can alter example semantics and move generated graphs off the data manifold, resulting in sub-optimal performance.

contributions.claim: MotifCAR combines one graph's motif with another graph's contextual subgraph to produce a raw counterfactual graph.
A GAN-based graph optimizer refines raw counterfactual graphs using adversarial guidance, motif consistency, contextual loss, and connection loss.
The refinement objectives target Realism, Validity, Proximity, and Sparsity in generated counterfactual graphs.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present MotifCAR as a novel approach for graph-level anomaly detection.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that MotifCAR can generate high-quality counterfactual graphs.
The authors report that experiments demonstrate MotifCAR's superiority.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph-level anomaly detection is important across diverse domains, and counterfactual graphs are used to improve generalization by learning causal relations.
Direct perturbations used by existing methods may change semantics and produce graphs off the data manifold.
MotifCAR constructs raw counterfactuals by combining a motif from one graph with the contextual subgraph of another, then refines them with a GAN-based graph optimizer.
Adversarial, motif-consistency, contextual, and connection objectives target realism, validity, proximity, and sparsity.
The authors report high-quality counterfactual graphs and experimental superiority.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and numerical experiment results are not provided.
The abstract does not specify the GAN architecture, training procedure, or computational requirements.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported superiority.
